approachQuestion.prompt:
Balanced Loads

A read-only nondecreasing array loads contains signed integer load changes. Return every distinct value triple [a,b,c] with a<=b<=c and a+b+c=0 that can be drawn from three distinct input positions. Multiplicity matters for availability, but each value triple appears once. Return the triples in lexicographic order.

Constraints: 0 <= n = loads.length <= 3000; -1000000000 <= loads[i] <= 1000000000. Use signed 64-bit sums.

Example 1: loads=[-3,-1,-1,0,1,2,3] -> [[-3,0,3],[-3,1,2],[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]].
Example 2: loads=[0,0,0,0] -> [[0,0,0]].
Example 3: loads=[-2,1] -> [].
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Process each distinct anchor value at index i in increasing order. Search indices i+1 through n-1 from opposite ends: increase left for a negative triple sum, decrease right for a positive sum, and on zero emit the triple once and skip both equal endpoint runs.
options.feedback: Every triple has a first value. Duplicate anchors and equal endpoint runs suppress repeated value triples without losing required multiplicities.

options.text: For every distinct anchor and every later distinct second value, binary-search for the needed third value strictly after that second position. Emit each found triple once in loop order.
options.feedback: This is correct and ordered, but independently searches for each third value instead of reusing the monotone pair boundary.

options.text: Remove duplicate values first, then enumerate triples of distinct values whose sum is zero.
options.feedback: For [0,0,0], the required triple uses three copies of one value and is lost.

options.text: For each anchor, compare opposite endpoints of the suffix and move both inward after every comparison, emitting only if the sum is zero.
options.feedback: For [-4,0,1,3], it first sees -4+0+3<0 and discards the 3 before finding the valid [-4,1,3].

feedback.reason: Fix one value and solve a residual pair relation while separately handling duplicate anchors and duplicate pair runs.
details: Visit each anchor index with at least two later positions, skipping anchors equal to the previous anchor. Set left=i+1 and right=n-1. Move left when the triple sum is negative and right when positive. On zero, append the triple, then advance both past their equal-value runs. Process all anchors in order.

For a fixed anchor, a negative sum requires a larger left value and a positive sum requires a smaller right value. Skip equal runs after a match to avoid duplicate value triples while retaining distinct index candidates during the search.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n is input length. Append output triples to a returned growable list with amortized constant-time append; occasional output-list copying is included in time and treated as output storage. All fixed-method scans are iterative; no auxiliary set, copied input, hashing, or recursion.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(n² log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each anchor performs a linear suffix sweep, giving quadratic worst-case work.
details: For each of at most n anchors, the suffix scan advances each endpoint at most n times, giving O(n²) time. All-positive distinct values force suffix scans of decreasing linear lengths, establishing the quadratic worst case even with no output. The output triples are excluded; only anchor and endpoint state remains.

“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The suffix scan repeats for many different anchors.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The method does not allocate a deduplication table or copied input.
“O(n² log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes independent searches for third values, not the fixed pair scan.
